title: Code Listen Cursor
user: A developer with reading fatigue, dyslexia, low vision, or an auditory workflow who needs an editor selection read aloud as intelligible code while maintaining cursor-level control.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A current feature request asks for right-click text-to-speech for selected terminal text or a summary, directly naming a developer reading need.
A 57-reaction request asks for voice transcription in a TUI, confirming current demand for voice-first interaction in terminal-based coding workflows.

recurrence: Code-specific text-to-speech and adjustable editor presentation are separate signs that source code needs individual reading controls.
current_workaround: Use generic OS text-to-speech that pronounces punctuation poorly, copy code into another app, or only enlarge the entire editor.
incumbents_and_gap: VS Code accessibility features, NVDA, VoiceOver, and Read Aloud extensions exist; a small tool that follows the active selection and gives user-tunable code pronunciation/structure without changing the editor is missing.
smallest_useful_product: A VS Code extension that reads selected code or the current line using language-aware punctuation rules, exposes cursor-follow and repeat shortcuts, and supports a personal pronunciation map. Non-goals: code generation, cloud voice cloning, IDE replacement, or code upload.
success_measure: Every shipped structural-cue fixture produces its expected spoken symbol and indentation cue in an independent sandbox run.
constraints: Use only speech voices marked local by the browser or editor unless a person explicitly chooses otherwise; keep source out of product network requests and storage; keep controls keyboard-operable and shortcuts configurable.
why_distinct: It solves listening to the current code structure and cursor context, not generic document narration.
